standard_prerequisites.name: The beta function lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Regularity of the minimised predicate: for every prefix of the recursion there is a sequence code d realising it, so the minimum exists.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 1590-1596): h defined by primitive recursion from total computable f, g is computable.

Auxiliary construction (proof lines 1598-1622): define h-hat(vec x, y) = mu d (beta(d,0) = f(vec x) and forall i < y, beta(d,i+1) = g(vec x, i, beta(d,i))), the least code of the recursion's value sequence;
the minimised predicate is regular by the beta-function lemma stub (no primitive recursion needed, only minimization);
h(vec x, y) = beta(h-hat(vec x, y), y), so h is built from basic functions by composition and regular minimization.
proof_roadmap: Code the recursion's history as a sequence via the beta function.
Define h-hat by regular minimization over sequence codes.
Extract h as the beta projection at y.
difficulty_reason: Primitive-recursion closure (statement 1590-1596, proof 1598-1622): a complete coding construction (sequence code, regularity via the beta stub, projection). H2.
